workload.description: Photo-first social app; media delivery dominates traffic, media processing dominates compute

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.r6g.large — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

db.r6g.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.225/h Single-AZ x 730 = 16425c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class. A read replica is billed as its own full instance, at the same rate as a primary.

citations.note: $0.0725/h x 730 = 5293c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 15,000 req/s peak. Mix: 42% feed scroll, 38% media fetch, 13% profile/explore, 6% engagement, 1% upload (~150 uploads/s peak, ~4.3M posts/day at average load)

assumptions.subject: media
assumptions.statement: One upload produces ~4 image renditions, or a short-video transcode. A 2-vCPU ARM instance clears ~12 uploads/s of that work. This is the busiest component in the design and the reason the fleet is 18 instances for a 1%-of-traffic flow

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: CDN hit-rate 90% on media; ~150 KB average delivered object across the feed-thumbnail / full-size / video-segment mix

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Feed cache hit-rate 85%; profile/explore 60%. Instance count (2) is set by working-set MEMORY and HA, not rps

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The SQL primary is modelled as ONE instance because there is one writer. A Multi-AZ standby is assumed in a real deployment but is NOT modelled as a second instance: it serves no traffic, and the engine would credit it with capacity it does not have. The engine will therefore flag the primary as a single point of failure - that flag is correct about failover, not about capacity.

assumptions.subject: api
assumptions.statement: API tier ~1,800 rps/instance (feed assembly from cache plus signed media URLs)

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: 800 TB: originals plus all renditions for ~6 months of uploads at ~4.3M/day

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Monthly usage volumes (egress/storage/requests) are derived from AVERAGE load = peak / 3; capacity and instance counts are sized to PEAK. A single system_rps cannot carry both, so the peak:average ratio is stated here rather than hidden in a volume.

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Delivery egress is priced at the model's single flat internet-egress rate ($0.09/GB, the US first paid tier). At the petabyte-per-month volume this design implies, a real committed CDN contract is roughly 5-10x cheaper, so the egress line is an UPPER BOUND, not a quote. The volume (GB/month) is the engineering claim; the rate is not negotiated here.

assumptions.subject: scope
assumptions.statement: Stories, DMs, Reels ranking and the recommendation model are OUT of this reference. Explore is modelled as a cached read, not as a live ranking call

_library.summary: Photo-first social app where media delivery dominates traffic and rendition processing dominates compute.
